title: Interleaved decode checkpoint reconciliation and kernel fallthrough strategy
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: In production we observe intermittent decode correctness/regression windows when CUDA Graph captures occur concurrently across interleaved decode streams. Root causes are a combination of non-deterministic kernel code paths chosen at capture time, subtle differences in prefill timing, and racey KV cache warmup. This ticket scopes a robust reconciliation approach that: (1) detects divergence between a captured graph's execution and the expected sequence state, (2) provides a safe fallback (kernel fallthrough) to an alternate deterministic execution path without significant latency/regression for common cases, and (3) adds lightweight runtime checks and diagnostics to prevent silent correctness issues.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New reconciliation layer can detect sequence/state divergence within <=1ms of replay for 99% of synthetic divergence cases.
2) Kernel fallthrough path executes correctly and returns identical logits/top-k to the primary capture in >99.9% of non-divergent cases.
3) No tail-latency regression >5% p95 for decode workloads when reconciliation is enabled.
4) Clear telemetry exposed in Console: divergence_count, fallthrough_count, avg_reconciliation_latency.
5) Automated fuzz tests added to CI that reproduce previously observed race patterns.
implementation_plan:
Phase A - Safe detection (3 days): add per-stream lightweight deterministic checksum of key tensors at prefill boundary and after KV apply; instrument capture code to emit checksums into the graph metadata. Run microbench harness to collect false-positive rate.
Phase B - Fallthrough execution (3 days): implement an alternate path that bypasses the CUDA-graph replay and executes a vetted sequence of kernels (deterministic reference path). Fallthrough should be fast-path optimized (reduced memory copies, kernel fusion where safe).
Phase C - Orchestration & rollouts (2 days): add policy to trigger fallthrough on checksum mismatch or capture-validation failure. Add canary config (10% traffic) and rollback hooks.
Phase D - Observability & tests (2 days): add dashboard widgets and CI fuzz harness that schedules interleaved captures with varying prefill offsets. Finalize perf guardrails and feature flag default-off for initial rollout.
risks: Increased code complexity could introduce new regressions if alternate kernels differ subtly in numerics
False positives from checksum heuristics could cause unnecessary fallthroughs and cost increase
Performance impact on p95 if reconciliation is too aggressive; must tune thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for checksum generator and validator (deterministic across seeds)
Integration test that simulates multiple overlapping captures with shifted prefill windows and verifies end-to-end logits equality or graceful fallback
Load test with production-like request distributions to measure p50/p95/p99 latency changes with reconciliation enabled
Fuzz harness that mutates KV timing to attempt to break capture assumptions
notes: Reference: kernel fallthrough prototype by S. Gupta (PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/7198)
